title: Classify: the main module and its nested tools
description: Choose image or measurement-based classification, start from downloadable examples, inspect real results, and find the five tools now nested inside Classify.
objectives: Choose the classifier family from the unified Home module.
Use the linked real-data CV and tabular lessons with their explicit limitations.
Find Classifier Evaluation, Explain CV, Activation, Training Runs and Feature Explorer under Classify.
Keep saved evidence and distinguish AI assistance from verified analysis.
prerequisite: Recorded with spaCR 1.5.0.6. The main-module section contains this overview; specialized and nested lessons remain grouped under Classify in the submodule section. This overview reuses genuine, previously verified CV and ML recordings rather than rerunning models. They use DIFFERENT labels and example subsets and are NOT a head-to-head benchmark. Tabular example: Load test data → Load; measured cells, metadata classes columnID=c1/c2, random forest, Plot on, 2153 scored objects and 188 unscored objects missing nucleus data; actual test wells are separate but share one plate. CV example: the linked lesson explicitly prepares 64 unchanged downloaded annotated crops with canonical database filenames, Generate training dataset off, ResNet18 for one epoch, 16 train/16 validation/32 test, disjoint actual wells on one plate, accuracy 0.5 equal to the majority baseline. The old filename parser is not repaired. Follow the specialized lessons for reproducible settings, saved paths and limitations. Current nested routes: classifier_evaluation, explain_cv, activation, train_compare, feature_explorer. Explain CV fits measured features to existing CV predictions; it is not proof of causality. Activation visualizes image-model responses. No AI request, new model-quality claim, biological validation or direct family comparison is made. API: spacr.classify.classify dispatches by classifier_family to spacr.deep_spacr.train_test_model or spacr.ml.generate_ml_scores.

scenes.narration: Classify is one of the main modules on Home. Open it here, then choose your classifier family inside the module. The tutorial player follows the same structure: this overview belongs to main modules, while specialized workflows and nested tools are grouped under Classify in the submodule section.

Computer Vision uses object images; Tabular Machine Learning uses saved measurements. Choose according to your inputs and scientific question, not the name that sounds more powerful. Changing family does not redo segmentation. The linked Mask and Measure lessons cover their own live image and crop controls.

For the tabular example, click Load test data and choose Load rather than Stream. Keep the downloaded project and measurements database together. For your own images, complete measurement first. The detailed tabular lesson records the actual download, label choices, settings and completed random-forest run.

These are that real run's plots and console, with Plot enabled. Its teaching labels are plate columns, not independently validated phenotypes. Objects missing required nucleus data remain unscored, not negative. Inspect saved predictions and the held-out wells; colourful figures alone do not establish generalization to another experiment.

The separate computer-vision lesson uses an explicit filename-preparation workaround and sixty-four unchanged downloaded crops. Its one-epoch model achieves only the majority baseline. These two examples use different labels and subsets; do not compare their accuracies as a benchmark. Follow the linked lesson before preparing your own split.

The icons at the top right open nested tools, not separate Home tiles. Hover to identify each one. Classifier Evaluation is for inspecting a saved evaluation bundle, including predictions and leakage information. Its own lesson explains the required files and why a displayed metric still needs a sound validation design.

Explain CV uses measured features to model existing computer-vision predictions. It is a separate explanatory model, not the original image network and not a causal explanation. Its tutorial shows the correct prediction input and the available results. Do not assume tabular-classifier outputs satisfy that input contract.

Activation opens the image-model interpretation workflow. Use the matching checkpoint, image channels and preprocessing. The linked tutorial demonstrates genuine saved saliency maps and explains its external-viewer workaround. A highlighted image region is not proof of biological mechanism or of a well-performing classifier.

Training Runs compares saved training histories and settings. It does not create independent evidence merely by putting two curves together. Keep runs in separate preserved directories and compare compatible metrics and data splits. Its dedicated tutorial covers the controls without repeating them in this main-module overview.

Feature Explorer opens directly from the final icon. It can rank measured features for a chosen comparison before a classifier is trained. Its lesson uses the real downloaded measurements and demonstrates live filters. Check the selected comparison again after filtering; a ranking is neither causality nor a trained image model.

The console also offers optional spaCR AI assistance. Here the question is unsent; no provider response or analysis result is demonstrated. Keep model outputs, settings and split evidence, and verify advice against them. In Python, classify dispatches to the image or tabular implementation selected by classifier family.
